candidates.source_name: data.gov.sk — Národný katalóg otvorených dát (Slovak national open data catalogue)
candidates.why_relevant: Central Slovak open-data catalogue; the canonical discovery surface for any machine-readable dataset published by NBS, MF SR, ŠÚ SR or other public bodies touching payments, banking and cash. Organisation pages let you enumerate every dataset a publisher has ever registered, including retired ones whose live pages have disappeared.
candidates.legal_status: open data, typically CC-BY / open licence per dataset
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate organisations at /organization, then harvest dataset + distribution metadata via the DCAT-AP-SK interface (legacy CKAN API still present but deprecated); snapshot dataset lists periodically to detect retired series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from MIRRI open-data pages
queries_used: data.gov.sk otvorené dáta Národná banka Slovenska platby dataset
data.gov.sk katalóg datasetov "Národná banka Slovenska" API CKAN DCAT

candidates.source_name: data.slovensko.sk — Národný katalóg otvorených dát (successor portal) + SPARQL endpoint
candidates.why_relevant: Successor/parallel front-end of the national catalogue exposing DCAT-AP-SK 3.0 metadata via a SPARQL endpoint — the most machine-friendly way to query the whole Slovak public-sector dataset inventory for payment/banking keywords, and to track when a distribution URL changes or disappears.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SPARQL queries against /sparql filtered on dcat:keyword / publisher = NBS, MF SR, ŠÚ SR; store distribution accessURLs as ingestion targets.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from data.gov.sk / opendata.gov.sk methodology wiki
queries_used: data.gov.sk katalóg datasetov "Národná banka Slovenska" API CKAN DCAT

candidates.source_name: Metodika pre otvorené údaje (opendata.gov.sk Confluence) — API documentation for the national catalogue
candidates.why_relevant: Official methodology wiki documenting which machine interfaces the national catalogue offers (CKAN legacy vs DCAT-AP-SK), deprecation timelines, and publishing obligations. Essential for building a durable, non-breaking ingestion path and for knowing when an interface is being retired.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic fetch of the space index; diff pages describing API endpoints to detect interface changes.
queries_used: data.gov.sk katalóg datasetov "Národná banka Slovenska" API CKAN DCAT

candidates.source_name: NBS OpenStats — Národná banka Slovenska interactive statistics platform
candidates.why_relevant: NBS's own filter-and-download statistics layer (dashboards on banks, loans, deposits, expanding dataset selection). The most likely future home of machine-readable NBS payment/card series; contact statdata@nbs.sk is an explicit route to bulk data requests.
candidates.legal_status: public statistics, reuse with attribution presumed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Inspect the dashboard's underlying XHR/JSON calls for a stable data endpoint; otherwise scheduled export download. Email statdata@nbs.sk to ask whether an SDMX/REST endpoint exists.
queries_used: NBS SDMX API štatistické údaje stiahnutie dataset platobný styk
nbs.sk OpenStats API dataset payment statistics download

candidates.source_name: NBS — Časové rady vybraných ukazovateľov (time series of selected indicators, MFI statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Long-run downloadable time series (typically XLS) for Slovak monetary financial institutions — exactly the kind of file-based historical depth that survives site redesigns only if mirrored. Anchor for continuity when the interactive layer changes methodology.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the page for .xls/.xlsx/.csv links, mirror every vintage with retrieval date, and hash-diff to detect silent revisions.
queries_used: "nbs.sk" časové rady štatistické údaje xls download "platobné karty" bankomaty POS terminály

candidates.source_name: Legacy www.nbs.sk URL space (pre-redesign site paths still resolving, e.g. /sk/platby/platobne-systemy/...)
candidates.why_relevant: The old NBS information architecture (www.nbs.sk/sk/...) still appears in search indexes alongside the new nbs.sk/... paths. Legacy paths often carry older PDF/XLS releases and are the continuity bridge to Wayback captures of retired statistics pages.
candidates.source_subtype: retired site path / legacy URL space
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Maintain a legacy-URL map: for each old path record final resolved URL; where a path 404s, resolve the equivalent Wayback capture. Do not treat a single 404 as dead.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result comparison of old vs new URL patterns
queries_used: "nbs.sk" časové rady štatistické údaje xls download "platobné karty" bankomaty POS terminály

candidates.source_name: NBS SIPS payment system statistics (volume and value of transactions since 2003)
candidates.why_relevant: Continuous national retail payment system series running back to 1 January 2003 — one of the deepest Slovak payment time series available and a benchmark for detecting methodology breaks elsewhere.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Mirror all linked data files each release; keep every vintage for revision tracking.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search snowball from NBS statistics index
queries_used: nbs.sk OpenStats API dataset payment statistics download

candidates.source_name: NBS Štatistický bulletin (quarterly Statistical Bulletin PDF archive, since Oct 2011)
candidates.why_relevant: Quarterly PDF series published since October 2011 in Slovak and English. PDF releases freeze the data as published at the time — the only practical way to recover pre-revision vintages once online tables are overwritten.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate the full back-catalogue of issue PDFs, mirror them, and run table extraction only at analysis time (pointer-and-archive, not parse-on-collect).
queries_used: NBS "štatistický bulletin" archív PDF platobné karty bankomaty historické údaje

candidates.source_name: NBS Výročná správa (Annual Report) PDF back-catalogue
candidates.why_relevant: Annual reports carry payment-system, cash-circulation and card chapters with figures as published each year; the /_img/documents/_publikacie/ path is a stable, predictable document store that survives front-end redesigns.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Probe the predictable filename pattern (vsnbsNN.pdf) across years to reconstruct the full series without relying on the navigation.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result on nbs.sk document store
queries_used: web.archive.org nbs.sk statistika platobneho styku archived page

candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — captures of retired NBS / bank statistics pages
candidates.why_relevant: The only general-purpose surface preserving retired NBS statistics pages, discontinued card/ATM tables and pre-redesign PDF links. The CDX API allows programmatic enumeration of every capture of a URL prefix, making it the backbone of a continuity strategy for broken time series.
candidates.access_status: public but blocked for this agent's fetch tool
candidates.legal_status: archive copies of public pages; respect IA terms and rate limits
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the CDX API (http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=nbs.sk/*&output=json&collapse=urlkey) from the deterministic collector, not from the agent sandbox; then fetch id_ replays of the archived files.
queries_used: web.archive.org nbs.sk statistika platobneho styku archived page

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments Statistics datasets (PCP, PMC, and successor payment datasets) via SDMX 2.1 API
candidates.why_relevant: Harmonised, SK-broken-out card payment, cash withdrawal and fraud series with a documented SDMX 2.1 REST API and CSV/XLS/SDMX downloads. The single most ingestible machine-readable source for Slovak card/ATM/POS statistics, and immune to NBS site redesigns.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX 2.1 REST calls filtered on REF_AREA=SK; use data-discovery mode to enumerate dimensions, then pull full series with revision history.
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search + snowball from ECB help pages
queries_used: ECB Data Portal "PMI" payments statistics dataset SDMX series key card payments

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — PSS: Payments and Settlement Systems Statistics (DISCONTINUED, API-only)
candidates.why_relevant: The retired predecessor of the current ECB payment statistics, covering access/usage of payment services and terminals, TARGET2 per country and national retail systems, with Slovakia included. Explicitly not exposed in the portal UI and reachable only through the API — a textbook retired-series surface for a continuity cell, giving pre-methodology-break history that the current datasets no longer carry.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off full SDMX pull of the PSS dataflow for REF_AREA=SK and store as a frozen historical baseline; join to current PCP/PMC series and document the methodology break.
queries_used: ECB Data Portal SDMX API payment statistics dataset PSS Slovakia

candidates.source_name: Legacy ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (sdw.ecb.europa.eu) — Slovakia payments country tables
candidates.why_relevant: The retired SDW front-end (superseded by data.ecb.europa.eu) still surfaces in indexes with a Slovakia payments country-table node. Useful as a legacy-identifier map (old node/series keys → new dataset keys) and as a Wayback target where the old tables were laid out differently.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve redirects and record old-node → new-dataset mappings; for unresolvable nodes fall back to Wayback captures.
queries_used: data.europa.eu Slovakia payment statistics dataset harvested data.gov.sk

candidates.source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — DATAcube./STATdata public database API (data.statistics.sk/api/v2)
candidates.why_relevant: Fully documented public REST API over the Slovak statistical office's multidimensional cubes, returning JSON-stat/CSV/XML/XLSX/ODS. Provides household finance, retail turnover and ICT/e-commerce context series for cash-vs-card behaviour, and a collection endpoint that enumerates every available cube — including ones being migrated or retired.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Pull /api/v2/collection?lang=en to inventory cubes, then /api/v2/dataset/{cube}/... in JSON-stat. Respect the 10,000-item and 2,000-character URL limits; refresh after the 10:00/22:00 daily updates.
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search + fetch of the API help page

candidates.source_name: DATAcube → STATdata migration (dual-running legacy and successor SK statistical databases)
candidates.why_relevant: ŠÚ SR is migrating the whole DATAcube database into a new STATdata platform, with new cubes created only in the new system while both run in parallel. This is an active continuity risk and opportunity: cube identifiers and URLs will change, and the legacy database is the vintage of record until it is switched off.

negative_findings.description: WebFetch could not reach web.archive.org at all: the CDX query for nbs.sk/sk/statisticke-udaje* returned 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org'.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Wayback captures could be enumerated or inspected during this run. This is an agent-side egress restriction, NOT evidence that the archive or the captures are unavailable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Wayback Machine is the load-bearing surface for this coverage cell (retired NBS statistics pages, pre-redesign PDF links). The deterministic collector must exercise the CDX API from an unrestricted environment before any conclusion is drawn about historical coverage depth.

negative_findings.description: No public SDMX or REST endpoint for NBS statistics was found. The OpenStats page documents interactive filtering and download but states no API; NBS procurement documents describe an Open Data solution 'with the use of API' but no live endpoint URL surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: NBS machine-readable access appears to be file-download and dashboard-export only at present; SDMX for SK payment aggregates is available only via the ECB, not NBS directly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ingestion plans must not assume an NBS SDMX endpoint. The ECB Data Portal is the practical SDMX route for SK payment/card series, with NBS files as the national-detail supplement. Worth an explicit enquiry to statdata@nbs.sk.

negative_findings.description: archiv.nbs.sk was hypothesised to host the retired pre-redesign NBS website. Fetching the site showed it is exclusively the institutional/physical archive (archival fonds, library, researcher portal) with no statistics sections.
negative_findings.result_summary: archiv.nbs.sk is not a mirror of the old NBS web statistics; it is a records archive under act 395/2002.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents wasted crawling effort and mis-scoped expectations; the retired-page problem must be solved via Wayback plus legacy www.nbs.sk paths, not via archiv.nbs.sk.

negative_findings.description: Slovakia is not a member jurisdiction of the CPMI, so the BIS Red Book / data.bis.org CPMI tables do not carry Slovak country data despite one search summary implying otherwise.
negative_findings.result_summary: BIS CPMI is a comparator and methodology source for SK, not a data source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids a fabricated data path; the CPMI methodology document (d168) remains useful for definitional alignment when reconciling SK series across ECB, IMF and NBS.

negative_findings.description: No specific payments/cards dataset published by NBS on data.gov.sk could be identified by name in this run; NBS is listed among catalogue organisations but the concrete dataset inventory was not enumerated (the organisation-scoped dataset listing was not fetched).
negative_findings.result_summary: NBS presence in the national catalogue is confirmed at organisation level only; dataset-level coverage remains unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The catalogue may hold either rich or near-empty NBS coverage; this determines whether data.gov.sk is a primary ingestion route or merely a discovery pointer. It should be resolved by a direct DCAT/SPARQL enumeration in the collection pass.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Slovak academic research-data repository (a Zenodo-style institutional data archive holding payment/banking microdata) was identified. Searches in Slovak surfaced only CRZP (theses) and CVTI SR library infrastructure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Academic data-repository coverage for SK payments appears thin; theses are the realistic academic long-tail surface.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Expectations for academic replication datasets on Slovak card/ATM usage should be low; effort is better spent on ECB/IMF machine-readable series and NBS PDF vintages.

coverage_gaps.description: The actual Wayback capture density for nbs.sk payment/card statistics URLs (how far back, how frequently, whether linked XLS/PDF files were captured or only HTML) is unknown because the archive was unreachable from this agent.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run CDX enumeration for nbs.sk/*, www.nbs.sk/sk/statisticke-udaje*, www.nbs.sk/sk/platby* and sbaonline.sk/* from the deterministic collector; record earliest capture, capture count and whether binary distributions were archived.

coverage_gaps.description: No crosswalk yet exists between retired and current series identifiers across the three continuity breaks identified: ECB PSS → PCP/PMC, ECB SDW nodes → data.ecb.europa.eu dataset keys, and ŠÚ SR DATAcube cube codes → STATdata codes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and store three explicit mapping tables with the methodology-break dates, so long series can be chained without silent discontinuities.

coverage_gaps.description: The dataset-level inventory of data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk for NBS, MF SR and ŠÚ SR under payment/banking keywords was not enumerated in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Execute a SPARQL/DCAT harvest filtered on publisher and on sk keywords (platby, platobné karty, bankomaty, hotovosť, banky) and store the result as a baseline snapshot for change detection.

coverage_gaps.description: Nothing found provides machine-readable Slovak payment/card series before roughly 2003 (SIPS) or 2011 (Statistical Bulletin). Koruna-era and early-2000s card/ATM data appear to exist only in paper or scanned form.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scope a one-off manual retrieval via the NBS Archive researcher portal (archiv.nbs.sk) and older Výročná správa PDFs if pre-euro baselines are analytically required; otherwise declare 2003 as the practical series start.

coverage_gaps.description: Whether NBS OpenStats exposes a stable underlying JSON/XHR data endpoint (as opposed to UI-only export) was not determined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Inspect network calls on the OpenStats dashboards from a browser-capable pass, and in parallel email statdata@nbs.sk asking about programmatic/bulk access and any SDMX plans.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovak-language searching for genuinely archival concepts ('archív štatistík', 'ukončená databáza', 'zrušená stránka') returned mostly current-page results; no Slovak-language index of retired statistical releases was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend local-language querying with publication-specific terms (e.g. 'Menový prehľad', 'Štatistický bulletin archív', 'Správa o platobnom styku') and with site-restricted queries against nbs.sk document paths (/_img/documents/).

brief: Slovakia's archival and machine-readable long tail for payments splits into three tiers. Tier one is supranational and genuinely API-first: the ECB Data Portal (SDMX 2.1, including the discontinued API-only PSS dataset that preserves pre-break payment/terminal history for SK) and the IMF FAS, plus the ŠÚ SR data.statistics.sk REST API for macro and household context — these are the only surfaces offering repeatable programmatic ingestion today. Tier two is national but file-based: NBS publishes time series, SIPS statistics since 2003, quarterly Štatistický bulletin PDFs since 2011 and Výročná správa PDFs from a predictable /_img/documents/ document store, with OpenStats as a dashboard layer and no evidenced public SDMX endpoint; the national catalogues data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk (DCAT-AP-SK, SPARQL) act as the discovery and continuity mirror. Tier three is recovery-only: Wayback captures of retired NBS and SBA pages, legacy www.nbs.sk paths, the NBS institutional archive (which holds records, not statistics), and CRZP theses that reproduce figures whose original sources are gone. Two live continuity risks dominate the cell — the ECB PSS/SDW retirement and the ongoing DATAcube-to-STATdata migration — and the Wayback Machine, the single most important surface here, was unreachable from this agent and must be exercised by the deterministic pass.
